name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield about 5.15% and 30-year 5.62% on 6 Nov, after the Bank of England's rate rise on 5 Nov
state: The 10-year gilt yield fell towards 5.1% on 6 Nov, its lowest since late August, before moving back above 5.15% after US jobs data (Trading Economics). The 30-year yield was 5.62% on 6 Nov, 36bp lower on the month but 36bp higher on the year. The Bank of England raised rates on 5 Nov, its first rise in over three years. The DMO has announced further operations, including a tender on 11 Nov; no weak auction or intervention was found, and Watch is kept as evidence does not clearly cross to Normal.
for_you: Gilt yields feed into government borrowing costs and the pricing of fixed-rate mortgages and annuities, so households and pension schemes tend to be the most exposed when long-dated yields stay elevated.
rubric_hit: 30y 5.62% still up 36bp on the year though down 36bp in a month; no weak auction or BoE intervention found. Watch held under hysteresis.

sources.title: UK Gilt Yields Fall as Flight to Safety Offsets Hawkish BoE Stance

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
